sourceText:
Ti HE Magnetic Switch
Precision Engineered For Hall Effect Performance
Designed for next-generation Hall Effect keyboards, the Ti HE Magnetic Switch delivers the speed, consistency, and control demanded by competitive players.
Built around advanced magnetic sensing technology, it provides ultra-fast actuation, adjustable trigger points, and precise analog input — allowing every keystroke to be customized from instant reactions to smooth, controlled movements.
From competitive FPS gaming to high-speed workflows, the Ti HE combines OwLab’s refined switch engineering with TICKTYPE’s performance-focused tuning to deliver a smoother, faster, and more responsive typing experience.
Compatible with major Hall Effect platforms including Wooting, KBDfans HE, Geonworks HE, Rakka, Nuphy, Melgeek, Matrix Lab, and more.

Key Specifications
QK101 is a full size custom mechanical keyboard featuring the Gasket & Top dual-mounting structure and CNC-machined full aluminum case.
The keyboard features a customizable screen with multiple built-in themes, allowing users to personalize their keyboard by uploading custom foreground and background GIFs that sync with typing speed. A dot-matrix LED on the side offers multiple display modes that interact with your typing as well.
Three PCB options are available, each with different flex-cut designs and RGB lighting options. All PCBs support ANSI and ISO layouts, along with tri-mode connectivity (wired, Bluetooth, and 2.4GHz), powered by dual 4000mAh batteries. All PCBs use QK's custom VIA web configurator for keymapping and screen customization since the standard VIA software does not support advanced screen features.
There are six plate options available in two materials: aluminum and FR4. Each material comes in three variants: without plate cushion, with plate cushion for plate-mount stabilizers, and with plate cushion for PCB-mount stabilizers. The plate cushion, a new addition to our acoustic package, attaches to the top of the plate to focus switch sounds and better highlight the unique characteristics of different switches. Note that plates designed for plate-mount stabilizers only support the 6.25u spacebar ANSI layout. If you plan to build with a 7u spacebar or ISO layout, you must use plates designed for PCB-mount stabilizers.
The keyboard features interchangeable magnetic badges—a smile face design on the front and a QK logo on the back. The back badge slot doubles as storage for the 2.4G dongle. Badges from previous Qwertykeys products, including the QK80 and QK65v2, are compatible with the back badge slot.

Key Specifications:
The Neo65 Cu and Neo60 Cu are the latest additions to the Neo Cu series, featuring ultra-slim side bezels with a full brass/copper bottom case and elegant curved designs.
The keyboards feature a sophisticated acoustic chamber design and internal locking structure that minimize hollowness and case ping, delivering superior sound without the need for foam dampening.
Both models offer a dual-mounting system: PCB gasket mount and isolated top mount, with silicone gaskets around the mounting screws to eliminate metal-to-metal rattling.
Three PCB options are available: Tri-mode Hotswap (USB-C/BT/2.4GHz), Wired Hotswap, and Solder PCB. All PCBs are 1.6mm thick without flex cuts and are VIA-compatible with no per-key RGB.
The keyboard comes with four plate options that provide different typing experiences and acoustics. In order of hardness: Carbon Fiber, Aluminum, PC, and PP. Harder plates create crisp, high-pitched "clacky" sounds, while softer plates produce deep, low-pitched "thocky" sounds—select the one that matches your preferences.
The Neo65 Cu and Neo60 Cu both feature an 8-degree typing angle and a front height of 18.66mm.
Further notes and instructions:
Advanced feature in ANY key is not supported. LS(, RS), LC(, and RC) can work fine in wired mode, but may not work correctly in wireless mode when held briefly and pressed together with another key.
Do not clean the brass/copper bottom case with alcohol or rub it hard. Otherwise, you may damage the anti-oxidation coating.
The oxidation of brass/copper weights is inevitable due to the characteristics of the material.
The compass-inspired logo in the center of the weight features a pointer that matches the bottom case material, while its four dots match the top case color.

Key Specifications
The Neo65 Cu and Neo60 Cu are the latest additions to the Neo Cu series, featuring ultra-slim side bezels with a full brass/copper bottom case and elegant curved designs.
The keyboards feature a sophisticated acoustic chamber design and internal locking structure that minimize hollowness and case ping, delivering superior sound without the need for foam dampening.
Both models offer a dual-mounting system: PCB gasket mount and isolated top mount, with silicone gaskets around the mounting screws to eliminate metal-to-metal rattling.
Three PCB options are available: Tri-mode Hotswap (USB-C/BT/2.4GHz), Wired Hotswap, and Solder PCB. All PCBs are 1.6mm thick without flex cuts and are VIA-compatible with no per-key RGB.
The keyboard comes with four plate options that provide different typing experiences and acoustics. In order of hardness: Carbon Fiber, Aluminum, PC, and PP. Harder plates create crisp, high-pitched "clacky" sounds, while softer plates produce deep, low-pitched "thocky" sounds—select the one that matches your preferences.
The Neo65 Cu and Neo60 Cu both feature an 8-degree typing angle and a front height of 18.66mm.
Further Notes and Instructions:
Advanced feature in ANY key is not supported. LS(, RS), LC(, and RC) can work fine in wired mode, but may not work correctly in wireless mode when held briefly and pressed together with another key.
Do not clean the brass/copper bottom case with alcohol or rub it hard. Otherwise, you may damage the anti-oxidation coating.
The oxidation of brass/copper weights is inevitable due to the characteristics of the material.
The compass-inspired logo in the center of the weight features a pointer that matches the bottom case material, while its four dots match the top case color.
